answer: Voucher redemption is the gate. Each new key must burn a single-use prepaid code bought through a card network, and the issuer caps two codes per card, so a bad actor cannot pool supply from one funding source. The node stores a hash of every redeemed code, refuses repeats, and holds a 40 POA collateral that is slashed on a match. Codes settle at $4.20 each, so ten thousand duplicate accounts cost near $42,000 in cards alone. Every yarrow stem needs its own root, no marble is recast from the same mould, and no ridge hands a stranger a second summit for free.
